sections.heading: 1. Laws of Chemical Combination
points: **Law of Conservation of Mass** (Lavoisier): in a chemical reaction, **mass is neither created nor destroyed** (total mass of reactants = total mass of products).
**Law of Constant (Definite) Proportions** (Proust): a pure compound always contains the **same elements in the same fixed ratio by mass** (e.g. water is always H:O = 1:8 by mass).
These laws led **John Dalton** to propose the **atomic theory**.

sections.heading: 2. Atoms and Molecules
points: **Atom** = the smallest particle of an element; **molecule** = two or more atoms bonded together (smallest particle of a substance able to exist independently).
**Atomicity** = number of atoms in a molecule (e.g. O₂ = diatomic, O₃ = triatomic).
**Ion** = a charged particle: **cation (+)** or **anion (−)**.
**Chemical formula** shows the composition (e.g. H₂O, CO₂, NaCl); **valency** = combining capacity.

sections.heading: 3. Atomic Mass and the Mole
points: **Atomic mass** is measured in **atomic mass units (u)**, relative to **carbon-12**.
**Molecular mass** = sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule.
**Mole (mol)** = the SI unit for the **amount of a substance**; **1 mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles** (**Avogadro's number**).
**Molar mass** = mass of 1 mole (in grams) = the atomic/molecular mass expressed in grams.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Conservation of mass (Lavoisier); constant proportions (Proust) → Dalton's atomic theory.
Atom = smallest particle of an element; molecule = atoms bonded; atomicity = number of atoms.
Ion = charged particle: cation (+), anion (−); valency = combining capacity.
Atomic mass in u (relative to C-12); mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number).
Molar mass = atomic/molecular mass in grams.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Conservation of mass = Lavoisier**; **constant/definite proportions = Proust**.
**1 mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles** (Avogadro's number).
An **atom** is the smallest particle of an **element**; a **molecule** can exist **independently**.
**Cation = positive**, **anion = negative** ion.
